en: I have carried this book in so many shapes and to so many places that in no way can I measure the debts accumulated along the way. My trail of paper and diskettes cannot adequately register why a particular scene became a relievo or when a particular argument became mine.
zh: 这本书以如此多的形态、被我带到如此多的地方，以至于我根本无法估量一路上欠下的债。我留下的纸张与磁盘的踪迹，无法充分说明为什么某个场景会凸显为浮雕般的亮点，也无法说明某个论点究竟何时变成了我自己的。

en: Time is not the only reason I cannot retrace all my debts: this book stands at the junction of emotive and intellectual communities that it straddles and unites without closure. Ernst and Hénock Trouillot influenced this project both during their lifetime and from beyond the grave in ways that are both transparent and intricate. I cannot date my interest in the production of history, but my first conscious marker is my perusal of the work they co-authored with Catts Pressoir, the first historiography book I read. They and other Haitian writers who preceded them are still privileged interlocutors at the boundaries of a custom-made intellectual community of relatives and friends I have in mind whatever I write. At the living center of that intellectual community, Michel Acacia, Pierre Buteau, Jean Coulanges, Lyonel Trouillot, Evelyne Trouillot-Ménard, and Drexel Woodson—who is too close to me and to Haiti not to be drafted into the family—have provided inspiration, comments, tips, and criticisms. I know that words are not enough, but mèsi anpil.
zh: 时间并不是我无法一一追溯这些债务的唯一原因：这本书站在情感共同体与知识共同体的交汇点上，它跨越并联结这些共同体，却不让它们闭合。恩斯特（Ernst）与埃诺克·特鲁约（Hénock Trouillot）生前和身后都影响着这项计划，其方式既清晰又错综。我无法确定自己对历史生产的兴趣始于何时，但第一个有意识的标记，是我细读他们与Catts Pressoir合著的那部书——那是我读的第一本史学史著作。他们以及先于他们的其他海地作家，至今仍是我最看重的对话者：无论我写什么，心里都装着一个由亲戚朋友组成的、为我量身定制的知识共同体，他们就站在这个共同体的边界上。在这个知识共同体活生生的中心，Michel Acacia、Pierre Buteau、Jean Coulanges、Lyonel Trouillot、Evelyne Trouillot-Ménard，以及Drexel Woodson——他同我和海地都太亲近了，不能不被算作家人——给了我灵感、评论、提示和批评。我知道言语不足以表达，但还是要说一声：mèsi anpil（海地克里奥尔语：多谢）。

en: I started to write on the production of history as a distinct topic in 1981. Some of these writings found a transcontinental community of debate in 1985 when David W. Cohen asked me to join the International Roundtable in History and Anthropology. My involvement in the Roundtables, my continuous and fruitful exchanges with other participants, including David himself, influenced my grasp of some of the issues treated here. Both chapters 1 and 2 evolved in different ways from papers I originally prepared for the Fifth and Sixth International Roundtables, respectively held in Paris in 1986 and Bellagio in 1989.
zh: 我从1981年开始把历史生产作为一个独立题目来写作。1985年，David W. Cohen邀我加入“历史与人类学国际圆桌会议”（International Roundtable in History and Anthropology），这些文字中的一部分由此找到了一个跨洲的讨论共同体。我参与圆桌会议、与其他参与者（包括David本人）持续而富有成果的交流，影响了我对本书所处理的若干问题的把握。第一、二两章都以不同方式脱胎于我最初为第五、第六届国际圆桌会议准备的论文，那两届会议分别于1986年在巴黎、1989年在贝拉焦（Bellagio）举行。

en: Johns Hopkins University constitutes a third intellectual community that made this book possible. For the last six years, the Homewood campus provided my most demanding grounds for testing specific ideas: graduate and faculty seminars, and the most difficult audience to convince—students. Recurrent conversations in my theory classes, in the seminar on "The Perspective of the World," in the seminar in methodology in anthropology and history I taught with Sara Berry, and the general seminar of the Institute for Global Studies in Culture, Power and History helped me find the proper expression for many of the ideas exposed here. My colleague Sara S. Berry has been a generous intellectual companion, a stimulating source of ideas, and a sharp critic. Her formulations helped me to articulate some of my views. My colleagues in the Department of Anthropology during the years this book matured have been supportive friends and daily interlocutors: Eytan Bercovitch, Gillian Feeley-Harnik, Ashraf Ghani, Niloofar Haeri, Emily Martin, Sidney W. Mintz, Katherine Verdery, and, more recently, Yun-Xiang Yan. Sid's vast knowledge greatly improved chapter 4. Niloofar coached me on language matters, such as evidentials. Katherine commented on multiple versions of various chapters. Brackette F. Williams moved in as I was nearly finished but early enough to make the usual difference, especially in chapter 5. For the third time we were neighbors; for the third time, the intellectual landscape changed.
zh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学构成了使这本书成为可能的第三个知识共同体。过去六年里，霍姆伍德（Homewood）校区为我检验具体想法提供了最严苛的场地：研究生与教师的研讨课，以及最难说服的听众——学生。我的理论课上反复进行的讨论、“世界的视角”（The Perspective of the World）研讨课、我与Sara Berry合开的人类学与历史学方法论研讨课，以及“全球文化、权力与历史研究所”（Institute for Global Studies in Culture, Power and History）的常规研讨课，都帮我为这里的许多想法找到了恰当的表达。我的同事Sara S. Berry是一位慷慨的思想伴侣、一个激发灵感的源泉、一位犀利的批评者。她的表述帮助我厘清了自己的一些观点。在这本书酝酿成熟的岁月里，人类学系的同事们是支持我的朋友和日常的对话者：Eytan Bercovitch、Gillian Feeley-Harnik、Ashraf Ghani、Niloofar Haeri、Emily Martin、Sidney W. Mintz、Katherine Verdery，以及新近加入的阎云翔（Yun-Xiang Yan）。Sid的渊博学识大大改善了第四章。Niloofar在语言问题上指导过我，比如传信语（evidentials）。Katherine对各章的多个版本都提过意见。Brackette F. Williams在我接近完稿时到任，但仍来得及产生她惯常的影响，尤其是在第五章。这是我们第三次做邻居；第三次，知识图景随之改变。

en: I owe more to my students than they will ever know, the undergraduates from different classes and, especially, the Ph.D. candidates in anthropology and history who worked with me on issues that touched the production of history. Pamela Ballinger, April Hartfield, Fred Klaits, Kira Kosnick, Christopher McIntyre, Viranjini Munasinghe, Eric P. Rice, Hanan Sabea, and Nathalie Zacek are among those whose reactions to my ideas and specific comments on parts of this book forced me to revisit points I thought obvious.
zh: 我欠学生们的，比他们所能知道的更多——各门课上的本科生，尤其是与我一起探讨涉及历史生产问题的人类学与历史学博士候选人。Pamela Ballinger、April Hartfield、Fred Klaits、Kira Kosnick、Christopher McIntyre、Viranjini Munasinghe、Eric P. Rice、Hanan Sabea、Nathalie Zacek都在其列：他们对我的想法的反应、对本书部分章节的具体意见，迫使我重新审视那些我原以为不言自明的地方。

en: Previous versions of parts of this book were published in Public Culture and the Journal of Caribbean History. I thank both publications for the opportunity of publishing these earlier articles and for the permission to reprint here. I also presented parts of this book in a number of academic settings: the International Roundtables in History and Anthropology, the conference "Révolution Haïtienne et Révolution Française" (Port-au-Prince, Haiti, 12 December 1989), and various seminars at Harvard, the University of Michigan, the University of Pennsylvania, and Johns Hopkins University. In each case, I benefited from stimulating discussions. David W. Cohen, Joan DeJean, Nancy Farriss, Dorothy Ross, Doris Sommer, Rebecca Scott, and William Rowe deserve special thanks for making these encounters both possible and fruitful. I also thank the institutions mentioned, as well as the Maison des Sciences de l'Homme, Paris, and the Max Plank Institut, Göttingen, which cosponsored the Roundtables.
zh: 本书部分内容的先前版本曾发表于《公共文化》（Public Culture）和《加勒比历史杂志》（Journal of Caribbean History）。感谢这两家刊物给我发表这些早期文章的机会，并允许在此重印。我还在一些学术场合报告过本书的部分内容：历史与人类学国际圆桌会议、“海地革命与法国大革命”（Révolution Haïtienne et Révolution Française）研讨会（海地太子港，1989年12月12日），以及哈佛、密歇根大学、宾夕法尼亚大学和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的多场研讨课。每一次我都从富有启发的讨论中受益。David W. Cohen、Joan DeJean、Nancy Farriss、Dorothy Ross、Doris Sommer、Rebecca Scott、William Rowe值得特别感谢，是他们使这些交流成为可能并富有成果。我也要感谢上述各机构，以及共同主办圆桌会议的巴黎人文科学之家（Maison des Sciences de l'Homme）和哥廷根的“马克斯·普朗克研究所”（Max Plank Institut, Göttingen，原印如此）。

en: A number of institutions provided support for the research, writing, and editing that went into this book: the National Humanities Center, the John Simon Guggenheim Foundation, the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars, and Johns Hopkins University. Special thanks to Charles Blitzer who was twice a gracious host.
zh: 一些机构为本书的研究、写作和编辑提供了支持：全国人文中心（National Humanities Center）、约翰·西蒙·古根海姆基金会（John Simon Guggenheim Foundation）、伍德罗·威尔逊国际学者中心（Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars）和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学。特别感谢Charles Blitzer，他两度做东，盛情款待。

en: A number of individuals worked closely with me on the final version. Elizabeth Dunn provided research assistance on memory and commented on chapter 1. Anne-Carine Trouillot's comments were useful throughout and her help was crucial to chapter 4. Rebecca Bennette, Nadève Ménard, and Hilbert Shin commented on various parts of the final draft and assisted me both in research and throughout the final writing and editing. I thank them for having not rebelled more often. Special thanks to Hilbert Shin for protecting my research time. Deb Chasman, my editor at Beacon Press, nurtured this book with care and attention. Her extraordinary patience, her contagious enthusiasm, and her close collaboration made its completion possible. To Wendy Strothman, Ken Wong, Tisha Hooks, and the rest of the Beacon team, thanks also for sharing that enthusiasm. Warm thanks to Marlowe Bergendoff for her sensitive copy editing.
zh: 一些人与我密切合作，完成了最终稿。Elizabeth Dunn在记忆问题上提供了研究协助，并对第一章提了意见。Anne-Carine Trouillot的意见在全书各处都有用处，她的帮助对第四章至关重要。Rebecca Bennette、Nadève Ménard和Hilbert Shin对终稿各部分提了意见，并在研究和整个最终写作、编辑过程中协助我。感谢他们没有更频繁地“造反”。特别感谢Hilbert Shin保护了我的研究时间。我在Beacon Press的编辑Deb Chasman以细心和专注呵护了这本书。她非凡的耐心、富有感染力的热情和密切的合作，使它的完成成为可能。也要感谢Wendy Strothman、Ken Wong、Tisha Hooks和Beacon团队的其他成员分享这份热情。衷心感谢Marlowe Bergendoff细致的文字编辑。

en: Both within and beyond the boundaries of these overlapping communities of labor, interest, and emotion, a number of individuals stand out for different reasons. From a vague suggestion that turned into a great lead, from a carefully written comment to a newspaper clip, or a document they took the pains to unearth especially for me, they have made subtle yet significant differences in the outcome. Some of them I have not yet named. Others will suffer an additional mention. Arjun Appadurai, Pamela Ballinger, Sara Berry, Carol A. Breckenridge, Pierre Buteau, David W. Cohen, Joan Dayan, Patrick Delatour, Daniel Elie, Nancy Farriss, Fred Klaits, Peter Hulme, Richard Kagan, Albert Mangones, Hans Medick, Sidney W. Mintz, Viranjini Munasinghe, Michèle Oriol, J. G. A. Pocock, Eric P. Rice, Hanan Sabea, Louis Sala-Molins, Gerald Sider, Gavin Smith, John Thornton, Anne-Carine Trouillot, Lyonel Trouillot, Katherine Verdery, Ronald Walters, and Drexel Woodson contributed to this book in various ways. Understandably, their input—and that of others—led to results they did not always intend.
zh: 在这些交叠的劳动、兴趣与情感共同体的边界内外，还有一些人因不同的原因而引人注目。从一条变成重要线索的模糊建议，到一份精心写下的评论、一张剪报，或一份他们特地为我费力发掘的文献，他们都对成果产生了微妙却重要的影响。有些人我还没有提到名字，另一些人则要再被提一次：Arjun Appadurai、Pamela Ballinger、Sara Berry、Carol A. Breckenridge、Pierre Buteau、David W. Cohen、Joan Dayan、Patrick Delatour、Daniel Elie、Nancy Farriss、Fred Klaits、Peter Hulme、Richard Kagan、Albert Mangones、Hans Medick、Sidney W. Mintz、Viranjini Munasinghe、Michèle Oriol、J. G. A. Pocock、Eric P. Rice、Hanan Sabea、Louis Sala-Molins、Gerald Sider、Gavin Smith、John Thornton、Anne-Carine Trouillot、Lyonel Trouillot、Katherine Verdery、Ronald Walters、Drexel Woodson，都以各种方式为这本书做了贡献。可以理解，他们的投入——以及其他人的投入——导致的结果并不总是他们所预期的。

en: I started these acknowledgments with family. I will also end there. My uncle, Lucien Morisset, provided a much-needed and idyllic retreat in Saint-Paul de Vence, where chapter 1 took definitive form and where the book finally emerged as a single whole. Anne-Carine and Canel Trouillot provided both the context of work and the context away from work. They added meaning to this and other ventures. I thank them for their presence and for mediating on the home front the pain and the perverse pleasure of writing in a second language.
zh: 这篇致谢以家人开始，也将以家人结束。我的舅父Lucien Morisset在圣保罗德旺斯（Saint-Paul de Vence）提供了一处急需的、田园诗般的隐居地，第一章在那里定型，全书也在那里最终成形为一个整体。Anne-Carine和Canel Trouillot既提供了工作的环境，也提供了工作之外的环境。他们为这项事业和其他事业增添了意义。感谢他们的陪伴，感谢他们在家庭这条战线上为我分担用第二语言写作的痛苦与那种反常的快乐。
